Vote counting and slot confirmation logic for notarized blocks.

# Purpose
This C file implements the `fd_notar` runtime object and its vote-processing logic. It defines the create, join, leave, and delete entry points for a notarization state that lives in shared memory, and it checks memory alignment, workspace membership, and allocation footprint before it initializes the internal block and voter tables. The [`fd_notar_new`](<#fd_notar_new>) function sets up the `fd_notar_t` object and its substructures, while [`fd_notar_join`](<#fd_notar_join>), [`fd_notar_leave`](<#fd_notar_leave>), and [`fd_notar_delete`](<#fd_notar_delete>) provide the standard lifecycle operations for attaching to and detaching from the shared-memory object.

The file also defines [`fd_notar_vote`](<#fd_notar_vote>), which records stake-weighted votes for slots in a tower and updates confirmation state for blocks. It filters votes by known voter, available replayed slot, and bank hash match, then counts stake for the last vote and, when the hash matches, for earlier tower votes that are valid in the current notar state. It marks blocks as propagation confirmed when stake reaches the `PRO_CONF` threshold and propagates that state to ancestor blocks on the same fork. The [`fd_notar_publish`](<#fd_notar_publish>) function advances the root slot and removes blocks below the new root from the notar state.
